## Prescription drugs Branded medicines with an

crowns and root canal treatment, is covered at 60 per cent up to 30,000 units
per policy year.

## Upgrades between plans A member upgrading from the Essential plan to the Premier plan serves a fresh
waiting period only for benefits that the Essential plan did not provide. For a
benefit that both plans provide at different levels, the member is covered at
the Essential level until the Premier waiting period for that benefit has been
served, and at the Premier level thereafter.

night.

A claim found to be fraudulent is declined in full. Aurora may in addition
cancel the policy from the date the fraudulent claim was submitted, in which
case benefits already paid in respect of that claim become repayable. Claims
unrelated to the fraud that were settled before that date are not reopened.

A member must notify Aurora of an inpatient admission within forty-eight hours
of the admission, or as soon as reasonably practicable where the member was
incapacitated. Failure to notify within the required period does not by itself
void the claim, but Aurora may reduce the settlement by 10 per cent of the
eligible amount where late notification has prevented it from managing the cost
of the episode. Every claim must include the completed claim form, the itemised invoice showing
the procedure codes applied, and the discharge summary where the claim relates
to an inpatient admission.

An approval states a maximum authorised amount; where the final cost

eligible amount by 30 per cent before applying the deductible and coinsurance.

eligible amount by 30 per cent before applying the deductible and coinsurance. The penalty is
waived where the member can show that the treating physician confirmed in
writing that the procedure was not one requiring pre-authorisation.

# Provider Network and Cashless Treatment ## Cashless treatment Cashless treatment is available only at a Tier One hospital and only with a
valid pre-authorisation.

## The allowed amount For an out-of-network provider the allowed amount is the lesser of the invoiced
charge and the median Tier One tariff for the same procedure code in the same
region. Where no Tier One tariff exists for the procedure code, the allowed
amount is the invoiced charge reduced by 25 per cent.

## Emergency admission to a non-network hospital An emergency admission to any hospital is reimbursed at the in-network rate for
the first seventy-two hours. The cost of a medically necessary transfer between hospitals is covered in full
under the Emergency Transport benefit and does not count toward the annual
benefit maximum.

Aurora may remove a hospital from the network at any time. Where a member has a
valid pre-authorisation for treatment at a hospital that is subsequently removed
from the network, the authorisation remains honoured at the in-network rate for
ninety days after the removal takes effect. At admission the member presents the membership card
and the authorisation reference.

# Maternity and Newborn Cover Maternity cover is provided under the Premier plan only. The Essential plan
covers complications of pregnancy as a general illness but does not cover
routine antenatal care or an uncomplicated delivery.

# Maternity and Newborn Cover Maternity benefits are available after the ten-month maternity waiting period
described in the Waiting Periods document. The waiting period is measured to the
date of delivery, not to the date of conception or the date of the first
antenatal appointment.

Two routine ultrasound scans per pregnancy
are covered, and further scans are covered where clinically indicated and
documented. An elective
caesarean section requested without clinical indication is covered up to the
same 180,000 units, with any excess borne by the member. A medically indicated
caesarean section is covered up to 320,000 units.

A medically indicated
caesarean section is covered up to 320,000 units. Complications of pregnancy and of delivery are covered under the member's
inpatient benefit and are not subject to the delivery limits above. For the
avoidance of doubt, a caesarean section performed in response to an emergent
complication during labour is treated as a complication and not as a delivery.

A newborn child is covered from birth for thirty days under the mother's policy
without a separate premium, whether or not the child is subsequently added to
the policy. This automatic cover is limited to 150,000 units. Where the child is added to the policy within thirty days of birth, cover
continues without interruption and no waiting period applies.

Generic medicines are covered at 90 per cent. Restorative dental work is not covered under the
Essential plan. spectacles and contact lenses are not covered.
